topic: Behavioral and senior ownership stories
scope: Today offers short spoken practice. Prepare real examples of ownership, failure/recovery, disagreement, ambiguity, mentoring, and measurable impact.
gaps: No fabricated stories or private career details are embedded. A dedicated behavioral recall deck is intentionally absent. Follow-up questions and truthful evidence need live practice.

topic: Mock interviews and communication under time pressure
scope: Explain assumptions, draw a full flow, trace code, test edge cases, and respond to changing requirements.
gaps: Content coverage and flashcard scores do not establish interview readiness. Use timed unseen coding, SQL, and design mocks with feedback.

topic: SQL Server runtime and concurrency verification
scope: Portable queries and expected results executed with SQLite; primary sources describe SQL Server differences.
gaps: No SQL Server engine was available. TOP/OFFSET, TRY/CATCH/XACT_ABORT, rowversion, locking, deadlock detection, execution-plan behavior, and native driver examples are source-reviewed only. Reproduce in a dedicated SQL Server sandbox.

topic: Advanced SQL and database operations
scope: After the 25-lesson foundation: recursive CTEs, INTERSECT/EXCEPT, advanced window frames, stored procedures, temp-table tuning, query parameter sensitivity, migrations, backup restore, and large-data plans.
gaps: Not a DBA certification or exhaustive T-SQL reference. Stored procedure/trigger authoring and engine administration are not fully taught.

topic: Advanced runtime and OS internals
scope: CPU caches and false sharing, memory-model proofs, lock-free algorithms, unsafe code, Span/Memory ownership, JIT/assembly, native interop, and deep GC tuning.
gaps: Fundamentals explain practical mechanisms; they do not replace role-specific performance engineering drills.

topic: Advanced distributed systems and specialist designs
scope: Consensus implementation, CRDT/OT correctness, multi-region write conflict algorithms, vector/search internals, stream processing watermarks, and storage-engine internals.
gaps: Common backend reasoning is covered first. Specialized role loops need targeted practice after company interview format is known.

topic: Company-specific loop preparation
scope: Confirm interview format and language, then prioritize its actual coding, SQL, design, debugging, and behavioral rounds.
gaps: No finite card deck covers every employer. Preserve short daily sessions and deepen weak areas based on evidence from mocks.
